headline: Govt keeps fuel prices unchanged for July
summary: The Ministry of Power, Energy and Mineral Resources has announced that the prices of all types of fuel will remain the same for the month of July.
details: The Bangladesh government has decided to keep the prices of all types of fuel unchanged for July. This decision follows the latest notification issued by the government on May 31.

According to a notification issued on Tuesday (June 30) by the Operation-1 branch of the Energy and Mineral Resources Division of the Ministry of Power, Energy and Mineral Resources, the current prices will remain in effect.
The consumer prices for diesel are set at 155 BDT per liter, octane at 145 BDT per liter, petrol at 140 BDT per liter, and kerosene at 135 BDT per liter.
These prices, which were established in the May 31 notification, will remain unchanged for the month of July and will be effective from July 1.
The government had previously increased fuel prices on the night of May 31, citing the global situation.

headline_marked: BNP supporters [[block Dhaka-Chattogram highway]] after Aslam Chowdhury's candidacy cancelled
headline: BNP supporters block Dhaka-Chattogram highway after Aslam Chowdhury's candidacy cancelled
summary: Protesters felled trees to block the road in Sitakunda following an Appellate Division ruling that declared the BNP candidate's nomination invalid.
details: BNP activists and supporters blocked the Dhaka-Chattogram highway at multiple locations in Sitakunda on Tuesday after learning that the candidacy of Aslam Chowdhury for the Chattogram-4 seat was cancelled by a court ruling.
The protesters created obstacles by felling trees across the road and holding processions and rallies between 12 PM and 3 PM at various points, including the Royal Cement Gate and Choto Darogarhat.
The Appellate Division delivered the verdict on Tuesday morning, granting an appeal by Jamaat-e-Islami candidate Anwar Siddiqui regarding the validity of Aslam Chowdhury's nomination.
Local BNP leaders stated they do not accept the ruling and claimed the cancellation was part of a 'black conspiracy' against Chowdhury, who they described as an honest leader.

Highway police from the Baraulia and Kumira stations eventually intervened, persuading the protesters to clear the road. Officials reported that the blockades lasted between 5 to 15 minutes at different locations.
Aslam Chowdhury's chief election agent, Md. Morsalin, stated that they intend to appeal the court's decision, asserting that Chowdhury's victory is inevitable despite the challenges.
